posts.title: The Download: Texas’s fragile AI boom and energy policy shifts
posts.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Texas was the new epicenter of the AI data center buildout. That might be kaput. Texas is the fastest-growing data center market in the US and ground zero for Big Tech’s…
bullets: Texas, previously the primary hub for hyperscale AI data center expansion, faces significant regulatory uncertainty following a major political shift that saw Democrats take control of the state government.
Data center development emerged as a decisive campaign issue, with voters rejecting such projects in 40 out of 41 midterm ballot measures and six cities moving to implement outright bans.

The political transition in Texas signals a broader national trend where the rapid AI infrastructure buildout is encountering localized political resistance, potentially stalling capital-intensive projects.
While federal climate legislation remains unlikely under the current administration, state-level policy shifts are becoming the primary drivers for energy grid management and data center viability.

posts.title: CATL, BYD gain EV battery share outside China as Korean rivals lose ground
posts.summary:
CATL and BYD's combined share rises to 44.5%, while the 6 Chinese makers in the top 10 hold 56.4%.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Chinese battery giants CATL and BYD captured a combined 44.5% market share outside of China in the first nine months of 2026, signaling a major shift in global supply chain dominance.
South Korean suppliers LGES, SK On, and Samsung SDI saw their combined market share drop to 26.5% as their North American battery usage volumes were halved.
CATL's international growth was bolstered by a 35.4% increase in European usage and the start of trial production at its Hungarian plant.
The data highlights a broader trend where Chinese manufacturers are successfully offsetting domestic saturation by aggressively expanding their footprint in European and Asian markets.

posts.title: BYD launches second-gen Seal 07 in China with lower prices and longer range
posts.summary:
The second-generation BYD Seal 07 features a larger body and a lower starting price of 139,900 yuan ($20,830).
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: BYD launched the second-generation Seal 07 with a starting price of 139,900 yuan, reflecting a 12% price reduction for the EV variant compared to the model released just eight months ago.
The new generation features significant dimensional increases, including an 85 mm longer body and a 60 mm longer wheelbase, enhancing interior space.
Performance upgrades include a 38-kWh battery for the DM-i plug-in hybrid, extending its electric-only range to 330 km, and a 76.744-kWh Blade Battery for the EV version, reaching a 775 km range.
The rapid product refresh cycle underscores BYD's aggressive strategy to maintain market share through constant price-to-performance improvements.

posts.title: A System-Level Approach To Protecting 3D-IC Signal Integrity
posts.summary:
Accurate SI analysis must account for interactions across vertical interconnects, interposers, silicon bridges, package transitions, and neighboring high-speed channels. 
The post A System-Level Approach To Protecting 3D-IC Signal Integrity appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: As chiplet-based architectures like CoWoS and EMIB become standard, traditional isolated die-level verification is insufficient to ensure signal integrity.
Advanced packaging introduces complex electromagnetic effects across vertical interconnects, TSVs, and silicon interposers that require holistic, system-level simulation.
Reliable communication in 2.5D/3D systems depends on mitigating impedance discontinuities and parasitic coupling that span across multiple process nodes and dense interconnect structures.

posts.title: Physical AI Pushes The Limits Of Hardware
posts.summary:
Autonomous machines promise to transform industries, but memory bottlenecks, power constraints, specialized architectures, and safety requirements are forcing chip designers to rethink the entire system.
The post Physical AI Pushes The Limits Of Hardware appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The physical AI market is projected to reach approximately €430 billion by 2030, driven by the need for autonomy in robotics, drones, and industrial systems.
Hardware designers are pivoting back toward highly optimized, application-specific ASICs to overcome the memory bandwidth and latency bottlenecks inherent in edge-based autonomous systems.
Addressing the technical challenges of physical AI requires a cross-disciplinary approach that balances power constraints, safety verification, and extended product lifespans.
